name: Ad-tech — click/install fraud, invalid-traffic (IVT)
parent_research_topic: Beava use cases — current and potential applications of beava as a real-time feature server

domain_fit.domain_name: Ad-tech click/install fraud and invalid-traffic (IVT) detection
domain_fit.one_line_definition: An ad-network, MMP, SSP/exchange, DSP, or advertiser must decide in single-digit-ms (pre-bid) to seconds (attribution-time) whether an inbound click, impression, or install is invalid (bot, click-flood, click-injection, SDK-spoof, device-farm, datacenter-IP, geo-mismatched) using per-click, per-device, per-publisher, per-sub-publisher rolling rates and distributions.
domain_fit.representative_jobs_to_be_done: Three concrete jobs: (1) Real-time pre-bid IVT filtering inside the SSP/exchange or DSP: in <10 ms of the bid-request roundtrip (HUMAN/White-Ops cites <=10 ms response), refuse to bid on impressions whose source IP, ASN, device-id, sub-publisher, or app-bundle has elevated rolling bot-rate, datacenter-IP rate, or duplicate-click rate. (2) Attribution-time install-fraud detection inside the MMP (AppsFlyer Protect360, Adjust Fraud Prevention Suite, Branch, Kochava, Singular): on every click and first-app-open, compute CTIT (click-to-install-time) distribution per publisher/sub-publisher, click-to-install ratio, install-velocity per device-id, and refuse-attribution / divert-payout for click-injection (CTIT <10 s), click-flooding (flat CTIT 2–24 h, low CTI ratio), SDK-spoofing (server-signature mismatch), and install-hijacking. (3) Post-impression / post-click batch reconciliation for advertisers and TAG/MRC reporting: produce per-campaign, per-publisher, per-placement IVT rates (GIVT and SIVT) compliant with MRC IVT Detection Guidelines and TAG Certified Against Fraud Guidelines (v7.3+), with auditable counters that can be reconciled against MMP raw logs for refund / clawback / publisher-credit workflows.
domain_fit.event_shapes: Typical events that would land in beava as @bv.event records: click {ts, click_id, campaign_id, creative_id, publisher_id, sub_publisher_id, network_id, device_id, ifa/idfa/gaid_hash, ip, ip_asn, ua_hash, geo_country, geo_city, app_bundle, placement_id}; impression {ts, imp_id, bid_id, campaign_id, publisher_id, app_bundle/site_domain, device_id, ip, ip_asn, ua_hash, viewable_ms, ssai_flag}; bid_request {ts, bid_id, exchange, publisher_id, app_bundle, ip, device_id, ua_hash, geo}; install / first_open {ts, install_id, app_id, device_id, ifa_hash, ip, geo, source_click_id, ctit_ms}; post_install_event {ts, install_id, event_name (registration, purchase, level_3), ttl_from_install_ms}; sdk_signature_check {ts, install_id, signature_valid (bool)}; attribution_decision {ts, install_id, attributed_publisher, decision (paid|rejected|fraud_code)}. Many shops also push pre-rolled signals (ip_is_datacenter, ip_is_residential_proxy, device_is_emulator) computed by an upstream IPQS / Fingerprint / HUMAN SDK. The adtech demo in the beava repo today only ships Impression / Click / Conversion (`python/beava/demos/adtech/schema.json`), so the fraud-specific event vocabulary would be a domain extension.
domain_fit.feature_shapes: Per-entity aggregations expressed in beava @bv.table primitives. Examples by entity: publisher_id and (publisher_id, sub_publisher_id) -> count(click, 1m/5m/1h/24h), count(install, 1h/24h), click-to-install-ratio = count(install)/count(click), CTIT distribution (t-digest or histogram with the 75% < 1h, 94% < 24h Branch / AppsFlyer benchmark as priors), share-of-datacenter-IPs (ratio), share-of-VPN/proxy-IPs, n_unique(device_id, 1h) for fan-out, n_unique(app_bundle, 24h); device_id / ifa_hash -> count(click, 1m/10m), n_unique(campaign_id, 1h), n_unique(publisher_id, 1h), time-since-last-install, install-velocity, CTIT for the device's last attributed install (click-injection signal when <10 s); ip -> count(click, 1m/10m), n_unique(device_id, 10m), n_unique(ifa_hash, 1h), datacenter-IP flag rate; (ip, app_bundle) -> count distinct devices; campaign_id -> rolling CTR distribution, rolling install/click ratio, rolling fraud-rejection rate; bid_id / imp_id -> idempotency tracking for no-double-count. Both exact (counters, ratios) and approximate (HLL n_unique for IP/device fan-out, CMS top-K offending sub-publishers, t-digest for CTIT and viewable-ms distributions) aggregates have legitimate roles — exact for the TAG/MRC reconciliation counters, approximate for the high-cardinality pre-bid filters where memory matters.
domain_fit.entity_grain: Highly multi-grain. Common primary keys: click_id, imp_id, bid_id (for idempotency); device_id / ifa_hash / idfa / gaid; ip; ua_hash; publisher_id and (publisher_id, sub_publisher_id) pair; campaign_id; (campaign_id, publisher_id) pair; app_bundle / site_domain; placement_id; (ip, app_bundle) pair for device-farm signals. A single pre-bid or attribution-time decision typically reads features from 5–10 of these grains.
domain_fit.window_semantics_required: All four. Sliding windows dominate (1m/5m/10m/1h for velocity and burst detection, 24h/7d for click-flooding which by construction looks flat 2–24 h post-click). Tumbling windows for MRC/TAG reporting (hourly / daily IVT rates per campaign/publisher). Session windows for per-device click bursts. Distribution aggregates (CTIT histogram, viewable-ms, click-cadence) are first-class — detection turns on the shape of the distribution, not just the count. Approximate sketches (HLL for n_unique IP/device, CMS for top-K offending publishers, t-digest for CTIT percentiles) are not just acceptable but preferred at exchange-scale where billions of bid requests per day make exact counts memory-prohibitive; exact counters are required only for the reconciliation/clawback path that must match MMP raw logs.
domain_fit.exactly_once_or_idempotency_needs: Strict no-double-count on the financially load-bearing counters: TAG-Certified IVT rates that drive refunds/clawbacks, per-campaign paid-install counts that drive CPI payouts, and per-publisher install attributions that drive sub-publisher revenue share. Idempotency keys are click_id / imp_id / install_id. The signal-feeding counters used by the pre-bid ML scorer tolerate at-least-once because a duplicate bot-click count does not change the bid decision materially.

technical_fit.latency_budget: Two regimes. Pre-bid (SSP/exchange/DSP filtering): the entire RTB auction is sub-100 ms end-to-end and the IVT-filter callout must return in <=10 ms (White Ops / HUMAN public spec). Attribution-time (MMP): seconds; AppsFlyer's distributed-microservices architecture is reported at 8–15 s attribution time, Adjust at 5–10 s. Beava's published sub-millisecond TCP get/batch_get fits comfortably inside both budgets.
technical_fit.feature_freshness_sla: Sub-second for pre-bid (a bot ring rotating IPs every 30 s makes a 1-min-stale rolling IP-bot-rate effectively useless). Single-digit seconds for attribution-time CTIT and click-flooding detection. Hours for batch IVT reconciliation. Beava's push-on-event ingestion gives single-digit-ms feature staleness, well inside the pre-bid window.
technical_fit.throughput_profile: Ad-tech is one of the highest-volume domains in computing. Public references: one major DSP at ~3M QPS / 2.5M sustained; bidscube/servers.com cite millions of bid requests per second at exchange scale; a typical large SSP processes billions of bid requests per day. TrafficGuard publicly cites 1 trillion+ data points/month. AppsFlyer reports up to 100k events/sec on its microservices fleet. Beava's published 684k EPS sustained on a single Apple-M4 core (TCP+msgpack+parallel=16) is enough for a mid-sized advertiser, a regional MMP tier, or a single SSP partition / DSP bidder shard; the largest global exchanges and MMPs would need horizontal sharding that beava v0 does not provide. [uncertain] exact per-vendor production EPS for HUMAN, Pixalate, DoubleVerify, TrafficGuard internal feature pipelines.
technical_fit.read_to_write_ratio: Write-heavy in pre-bid IVT filtering (every bid request writes to ip/device/publisher counters; only a sample reads the full feature vector when the rule actually fires); roughly balanced in MMP attribution (one click writes 5–10 counters and one batched read of 30–100 features). Card-flood / click-flood bursts skew strongly to write-heavy.
technical_fit.state_size_estimate: Order-of-magnitude per buyer: a mid-sized MMP tracking ~500M devices x 5 entity grains x 30 features x ~16 bytes ≈ 1.2 TB hot state — well above a single beava box. A single advertiser running per-campaign and per-publisher fraud rules on ~10M devices/day x 5 grains x 30 features x 16 bytes ≈ 24 GB — comfortably in-memory on a single beava box. A regional DSP bidder shard or a single SSP partition (the natural deployment unit) fits the single-binary model; the platform-wide global aggregate does not. This is exactly why HLL/CMS/t-digest sketches matter for this domain.
technical_fit.cardinality_pattern: Explosive on ip, ua_hash, device_id, and click_id (proxy pools, residential-proxy rotation, device-id reset farms, click-spam volumes). Bounded on campaign_id, creative_id, app_bundle, publisher_id. Slowly-growing on advertiser_id and network_id. The explosive grains are exactly where HLL n_unique, CMS top-K, and t-digest CTIT-distribution sketches are the right primitives; the bounded grains tolerate exact counters.
technical_fit.typical_state_lifecycle_and_ttl: Velocity counters: 1 min to 7 days (the 24-h click-flooding CTIT window plus a 7-day post-install attribution window are the natural ceilings). Per-publisher / per-sub-publisher reputation: 30–90 days. TAG/MRC IVT-rate reporting: quarterly tumbling counts retained 12–24 months for audit. Beava's WAL+snapshot suits the seconds-to-days hot tier; the 12–24-month audit tail belongs in a downstream warehouse.
technical_fit.typical_feature_count_per_decision: 30–500 features per decision. Production click-fraud models commonly use 200–500 features (per the real-time ML system design references). Pre-bid IVT scoring is often a thinner 20–50-feature decision because of the 10-ms budget. Beava's batch_get / get-many path is the right shape; ad-tech is one of the strongest demands on it.
technical_fit.durability_requirements: Mixed. The pre-bid ML-scoring path is best-effort: a brief WAL gap during a crash produces a small blind spot, fraudsters get a few thousand impressions through, and the cost is recoverable in batch reconciliation. The TAG-certified IVT-rate counters and the per-publisher payout reconciliation are regulator-/audit-grade and need durable storage with no double-count; beava's role is the hot-path aggregator and a durable downstream sink (warehouse, Kafka, S3) is required for the audit path. Beava's WAL+snapshot+refuse-on-network-FS posture matches the crash-safe tier.
technical_fit.deployment_topology_fit: Single-binary regional / single-binary-per-partition fits a DSP bidder shard, an SSP partition, a regional MMP node, or an advertiser-side IVT filter cleanly. Multi-region active-active for a global exchange does NOT fit today: beava has no in-process sharding and no cross-region replication in v0, so global ad networks cannot use a single beava as the source of truth. The MMP / SSP partitioned-by-customer-or-region pattern is the natural fit.

commercial_fit.who_buys: Multiple personas with distinct economics. (1) Mobile Measurement Partners (AppsFlyer, Adjust, Branch, Kochava, Singular) building Protect360 / Fraud Prevention Suite / Branch fraud detection — product/eng buyer. (2) SSPs and exchanges (PubMatic, Magnite, Index Exchange, OpenX) building pre-bid IVT filters or integrating HUMAN/Pixalate — platform-eng buyer. (3) DSPs (The Trade Desk, DV360, Amazon DSP) running budget-protection pre-bid filters — platform-eng buyer. (4) Verification vendors (HUMAN/White Ops, Pixalate, DoubleVerify, IAS) — their core product, infra-eng buyer. (5) Specialist click-fraud SaaS (ClickCease, TrafficGuard, Anura, Spider AF, ClickGuard, Fraud Blocker, Lunio) — SMB to mid-market, product-eng buyer. (6) Advertisers running in-house IVT filtering (large brands, gaming publishers) — growth/marketing-ops buyer. (7) CTV ad-platforms (Roku, FreeWheel, Amagi) — platform buyer.
commercial_fit.market_size_signal: Very large and growing. Public 2025–2026 estimates for global ad-fraud losses range from $32.6 B (Spider Labs / Yahoo Finance, 2025) to $84 B (2023) -> $100 B+ (2025) -> projected $172 B (2028); Fraudlogix puts global IVT at 20.64% of 105.7 B 2025 impressions analysed; Pixalate Q4 2025 puts global IVT at 23% web / 36% mobile-app / 21% CTV; US programmatic IVT loss estimated ~$37 B/yr. TAG awarded a record 326 Certified-Against-Fraud seals in 2025 and the 2024 US Fraud Savings Report (TAG + 4A's + ANA + IAB + IAB Tech Lab + MRC) put anti-fraud-standards savings at ~$11 B. Specialist click-fraud SaaS is a crowded but profitable niche — ClickCease alone has 14k+ customers across 106 countries. [uncertain] specific revenue for private vendors HUMAN, Pixalate, TrafficGuard, ClickCease (most are private and do not disclose ARR).
commercial_fit.urgency_drivers: Four forces. (1) Loss curve — ad-fraud losses growing double-digit % per year and concentrated in advertiser P&L (15–25% of digital ad spend is the cited industry range). (2) Regulation/standards — MRC IVT Detection and Filtration Guidelines 2024 interim updates push property-level reporting; TAG Certified Against Fraud v7.3 (2022) and 2025 platinum requirements raise the bar; CTV-specific MRC standards (2024) increase scrutiny on SSAI fraud. (3) AI ad-buying wave — 2025 saw fraud losses spike as generative-AI tools lowered fraudster cost-per-fake-click. (4) Attack-volume shift — sophisticated bot networks (residential-proxy rotation, real-device emulation, datacenter-IP rotation) now defeat naive GIVT filters; only SIVT detection with streaming features per device/IP/publisher catches them, which forces buyers to move from batch (T+1) to streaming (sub-second) feature pipelines.
commercial_fit.regulatory_or_audit_constraints: MRC IVT Detection and Filtration Standards (and 2024 interim update) — 100% of monetizable transactions must be filtered for GIVT and SIVT in a TAG-recognised way; counters must be auditable. TAG Certified Against Fraud v7.3 (2022) — explicit hot-path filtering + reporting + clawback workflow. IAB Tech Lab standards (app-ads.txt, sellers.json, SupplyChain Object, ads.cert) — reconciliation against beava state must align. GDPR / CCPA — ifa_hash, ip, device_id are personal data; retention TTLs and right-to-erasure apply; many MMPs require pseudonymisation. SOC 2 Type II is table stakes for enterprise customers. Beava's lack of TLS/auth in v0 is a blocker for buyer-side audit checklists.
commercial_fit.time_to_value_signal: A working per-publisher click-velocity and CTIT-distribution demo on synthetic events can stand up in roughly a day on beava given that `python/beava/demos/adtech/` already ships generic Impression/Click/Conversion. A realistic per-device/per-publisher/per-IP IVT scoring rig with 30–50 features fed by real click+install streams is a 1–3 week effort. A TAG-compliant production rig with auditable counters and clawback reconciliation takes a quarter or more because the audit, integration, and downstream-sink work dominates.

competition.incumbents: Two layers. (a) Generic streaming / feature-store platforms used to build ad-tech IVT rigs in-house: Redis (and Redis Cluster), Aerospike (well-suited for ad-tech scale, sub-ms latency at billions of records/day), Apache Kafka + Apache Flink, Materialize, RisingWave, Spark Structured Streaming / Spark Real-Time Mode, Confluent Flink, Tecton, Chalk, Fennel (Rust-based, ex-Facebook, explicitly markets to ad-tech), Hopsworks, Feast (often on Redis). (b) Custom-built systems on top of NoSQL / KV stores are extremely common at SSP/DSP/MMP scale because of the QPS profile. Beava competes most directly with the (Redis OR Aerospike) + (Flink OR Materialize) two-box pattern, by collapsing it into a single binary; against Fennel specifically, beava is a thinner single-binary alternative without the managed-cloud control plane.
competition.competitive_incumbent_per_domain: Domain-specific ad-tech anti-fraud platforms that buyers would otherwise procure as black boxes: HUMAN Security (ex-White Ops; MRC-accredited SIVT and pre-bid IVT), Pixalate (MRC-accredited IVT; pre-bid blocklists integrated into Amazon DSP, MoPub), DoubleVerify (MRC SIVT), Integral Ad Science (IAS), TrafficGuard (ASX-listed, mobile-fraud focused, 1T+ data points/month), Spider AF, ClickCease (14k+ SMB customers), ClickGuard, Fraud Blocker, Lunio, Anura, mFilterIt, Fraudlogix, ClickPatrol, ClickFortify. MMP-internal: AppsFlyer Protect360, Adjust Fraud Prevention Suite 2.0, Branch fraud detection, Kochava Fraud Console, Singular fraud-protection. CTV-specific: HUMAN MediaGuard, Pixalate CTV Compliance. Beava is not competing with these end-to-end products — it is the infrastructure layer that an MMP, SSP, DSP, or verification vendor would use to build or augment their own scorer, or that an advertiser would use to build an in-house IVT filter.
competition.beava_differentiator: Five concrete differentiators for this domain. (1) Single binary collapses Kafka+Flink+Redis+feature-store ETL into one box — ad-tech eng teams already run lean infra at the per-shard level, so removing 3 systems is a big win. (2) 50+ aggregation primitives including velocities, rates, distances, and distributions — click-fraud detection turns on distribution shape (CTIT, click-cadence, viewable-ms) and ratio aggregates (click-to-install) more than counts, which is exactly what beava ships. (3) Sub-ms TCP get/batch_get fits inside the 10-ms pre-bid IVT-filter budget with margin. (4) Push-on-event ingestion (HTTP/JSON, framed-TCP, msgpack) maps directly onto the way mobile SDKs and pixel servers already emit events — no Kafka assumption like Tecton/Feast/Hopsworks. (5) Apache-2.0 with no open-core split, which matters for verification vendors and MMPs who would otherwise have to negotiate against an enterprise-edition gate from a feature-store vendor.
competition.where_beava_loses_today: Concrete gaps that will block production ad-tech IVT deployments. (1) No TLS/auth on :8080/:8081/:8090 — a non-starter for SSP/DSP/MMP buyer security review even on a private subnet. (2) No in-process sharding — a global exchange's hot state cannot fit a single box; ad-tech is one of the strongest pulls for horizontal sharding. (3) No cross-region replication — multi-region MMPs cannot use beava as a single source of truth. (4) In-memory-only with refuse-on-network-FS — a node loss requires WAL replay, fraud blind spot for the duration, which the buyer must accept. (5) No triggers / no 'fire when counter crosses threshold' — anti-fraud teams want 'when publisher X's click-to-install ratio falls below T over W, automatically pause attribution payouts and emit a webhook' as a primitive, not a poll loop. (6) No multi-tenancy with namespace ACLs — a verification vendor cannot safely host multiple advertiser tenants on one beava box. (7) No first-class HLL / CMS / t-digest types yet documented externally; the '50+ primitives' claim covers some but not all of the sketches that explosive IP/device cardinality demands. (8) No native primitives for the GIVT/SIVT classification taxonomy, sub-publisher graph features, or sellers.json/SupplyChain-Object reconciliation — the buyer must build these on top. (9) The repo's adtech demo today is generic Impression/Click/Conversion, not fraud-shaped (`python/beava/demos/adtech/schema.json`); the bench workload (`crates/beava-bench/src/workloads/adtech.rs`) is explicitly described as a renamed `medium-with-sketches` config rather than a dedicated adtech-fraud workload.
competition.integration_surface: Upstream producers in this domain are heterogeneous: Kafka (large SSP/DSP backends), Kinesis (AWS-native shops), pixel-server HTTP push (the canonical impression/click event source), mobile SDK direct push (the canonical install event source — AppsFlyer/Adjust/Branch/Singular SDKs), prebid.js / bid-stream gRPC, exchange-side OpenRTB callouts, CDC streams from publisher-management Postgres. Beava's HTTP/JSON :8080 and framed-TCP :8081 (JSON or msgpack) maps cleanly to pixel-server and mobile-SDK paths; a thin Kafka/Kinesis consumer is required for the streaming paths and is not in v0. Downstream consumers: the ML scorer (XGBoost/LightGBM dominate, with 200–500 feature vectors per click; transformer-based models at the largest MMPs); the rules engine (per-publisher caps, datacenter-IP blocklists); the audit/clawback warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks).
competition.scoring_engine_coupling: Both. The buyer typically runs (a) a rules engine for MRC-/TAG-mandated hard cut-offs (datacenter-IP block, known-bad-fingerprint block, CTIT <10 s reject) and (b) an ML scorer (XGBoost/LightGBM, increasingly GNNs as ad-tech adopts NVIDIA-style fraud-graph models) that consumes beava features. Beava is the feature substrate under both.

adoption_signals.existing_public_users_or_case_studies: No publicly named beava users running this use case yet. Comparable published references that legitimise the shape: AppsFlyer Protect360 (ML trained on 500B+ events, real-time blocking at attribution-time, microservices fleet at up to 100k EPS); Adjust Fraud Prevention Suite 2.0 (real-time signature, click-injection filter, distribution modelling); TrafficGuard (1T+ data points/month, ASX-listed, mobile-MMP-native); HUMAN/White Ops (<=10 ms pre-bid response); Pixalate (integrated into Amazon DSP and MoPub for pre-bid IVT filtering); Caulis (Redis->Aerospike migration in a fraud-adjacent use case). The IVT verification vendor reference customers are extensive (Amazon DSP, MoPub, every major MMP/SSP) but the specific infrastructure under them is private. [uncertain] no public beava-named adtech-fraud case study identified in this research pass.
adoption_signals.community_discussions: [uncertain] Specific beava Discord / GitHub Discussion / RFC threads on click-fraud or IVT — the repo ships `python/beava/demos/adtech/schema.json` and a `crates/beava-bench/src/workloads/adtech.rs` workload, but those are generic Impression/Click/Conversion shapes and the workload file explicitly notes 'v0.1+ may ship a dedicated adtech config'. External community traction on adtech-fraud has not been verified through this research pass.
adoption_signals.examples_or_demos_in_repo: Partial. `python/beava/demos/adtech/schema.json` defines generic Impression / Click / Conversion events and `python/beava/demos/adtech/events.jsonl` ships a synthetic event stream; `crates/beava-bench/src/workloads/adtech.rs` runs the workload but is documented as 'backed by medium-with-sketches.json (Txn-style events with merchant_id) renamed for the adtech domain. v0.1+ may ship a dedicated adtech config (Impression / Click / Conversion).' No fraud-specific demo (CTIT distribution, click-flooding detection, SDK-spoofing signature check) ships in the repo today.
adoption_signals.adversarial_pressure_level: High / active adversary. Click-fraud and IVT are among the most adversarial domains in computing — fraudsters adapt to detection rules within hours, rotate IPs (residential proxies, ASN-shopping) and device IDs (limit-ad-tracking reset, emulator reset farms) continuously, reverse-engineer MMP SDKs (SDK-spoofing), and explicitly tune click-flood cadence to stay under per-publisher velocity thresholds. Feature drift, label drift, and concept drift are all aggressive. The 2025 generative-AI wave further lowered fraudster cost-per-fake-click.

risk_and_non_goals.non_goals: Beava is the wrong tool for: (1) Long historical look-backs (90+ day per-device fraud profiles for ML training — that belongs in a warehouse / offline feature store). (2) Full bid-request / impression archive for regulatory replay and 12–24-month TAG/MRC audit — belongs in S3/BigQuery/Snowflake; beava is the hot aggregator. (3) Cross-entity graph joins ('all installs in last 24 h where publisher.sellers_json_status = bad AND device.ifa IN (campaign_X devices)') — beava is keyed by primary entity, not a graph engine. (4) Batch model training and feature backfill (offline feature generation belongs in Spark/Snowflake/Databricks). (5) Long-tail device-graph / sub-publisher graph analytics (graph queries, not primary-key gets). (6) Verification-vendor multi-tenant hosting on one box (no namespace ACLs in v0). (7) The TAG/MRC audit-log itself — beava's WAL is replay-state, not an audit log of decisions made.
risk_and_non_goals.open_engineering_gaps: Concrete features beava would need to ship to be production-grade for ad-tech IVT at a mid-to-large MMP/SSP/DSP buyer: (1) TLS on all three listeners (:8080, :8081, :8090) plus mTLS. (2) AuthN/AuthZ — at minimum API-key auth scoped per namespace, ideally JWT/OIDC. (3) Triggers / event-driven actions — 'when (publisher_id, sub_publisher_id)'s click-to-install ratio drops below T over W or its datacenter-IP-share crosses U, emit an action event to a Kafka topic / webhook to pause payout' — this is the dominant ask of anti-fraud teams. (4) Multi-tenancy with hard namespace isolation, per-tenant quotas, per-tenant auth — verification vendors and MMPs are multi-tenant by definition. (5) In-process sharding and consistent-hashing on entity grain (ip, device_id, publisher_id) so a single global exchange's hot state can be partitioned. (6) Cross-region replication (active-active or active-passive with bounded staleness) for multi-region MMPs and global SSPs. (7) First-class probabilistic sketches surfaced as documented primitives: HLL for n_unique IP/device, CMS for top-K offending sub-publishers, t-digest for CTIT and viewable-ms distributions. (8) Native CTIT / time-since primitive that exposes percentile and histogram outputs cheaply (not just sum/count). (9) Secondary indexes or scan APIs for 'find top-N publishers by IVT rate in window W' (anti-fraud-ops dashboards, hunter queries). (10) Configurable per-feature TTLs so 90-day publisher reputations can coexist with 1-min IP velocity counters. (11) Explicit PII/token-field marking and audit log so the buyer can pass SOC 2 and MMP privacy review without manual evidence. (12) Durable downstream sink (Kafka/S3/Postgres CDC out) so TAG/MRC reconciliation and per-publisher clawback can be reconciled against a system of record. (13) A dedicated fraud-shaped adtech demo and bench workload in the repo (the current `adtech.rs` is a renamed `medium-with-sketches`; ad-tech buyers will want to see CTIT/click-flooding/SDK-spoofing primitives demonstrated end-to-end). (14) Optional native bindings for ip-asn / datacenter-IP / proxy-rep lookups, or first-class hooks so a HUMAN/Pixalate/IPQS enrichment can fan into a beava @bv.event.
risk_and_non_goals.trigger_action_required: Yes — strongly. Click-fraud and IVT are among the strongest pulls for the trigger/action gap. Anti-fraud teams want 'when (publisher, sub-publisher) CTI ratio collapses or CTIT distribution flattens between 2 and 24 h, emit a pause-payout action' and 'when device_id click-rate exceeds N in 1 min, emit a block action' as native primitives, not as poll loops. Adjust and AppsFlyer already block fraudulent installs in real time pre-attribution; beava would need a comparable trigger primitive to be a peer in the MMP-internal infrastructure layer.
